items.title: Waymo pauses robotaxi rides on US freeways after California ban
items.topic: Waymo pauses robotaxi rides on US freeways after California ban
items.summary: Headline tracked from Reuters as a recent automated vehicle signal.
items.abstract: Waymo has temporarily suspended or paused robotaxi operations in response to an incident or adverse conditions, illustrating that commercial AV services remain sensitive to edge-case failures. Such pauses are part of standard safety protocols in which operators pull vehicles until the cause is diagnosed and the system is updated or validated. The episode underscores the challenge of maintaining continuous commercial operations while meeting rigorous safety standards. It also provides real-world data that feeds back into improved fault-detection and operational-design-domain policies.

items.title: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
items.topic: Edge-Assisted Crowdsensing for Explainable Cyclist Safety Perception
items.summary: Cyclist fatality rates remain high despite policy support for active travel, and autonomous vehicles add complexity to mixed traffic. Neither crash statistics nor multi-model detection pipelines scale to continuous monitoring of perceived safety along a route. We present an edge-assisted crowdsensing system: handlebar cameras supply street-level frames, a vision-language model (VLM) turns each frame into structured traffic attributes through a single prompt, and an explainable boosting machine (EBM) combines them with OpenStreetMap road infrastructure and on-bike kinematics to predict a crowdsourced 1-9 safety score.

items.title: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
items.topic: FastRoverVLA: Fast Vision-Language-Action Execution for Off-Road Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Off-road vision-language-action (VLA) models generate scene-conditioned plans, but frequent trajectory updates can repeatedly invoke expensive multimodal inference. Reusing a prediction reduces this demand while leaving its commands exposed to changes in vehicle motion. FastRoverVLA addresses this mismatch by decoupling visual plan generation from motion-conditioned execution.

items.title: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
items.topic: Evaluating Video LLMs' Understanding of Corner Cases in Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Natural language explanations promised by modern Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) offer autonomous driving systems a path toward detailed scene description and interpretable decision making on the road.
